texts.preamble: M/S Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd. vs Food And Drug Administration Dewas on 15 January, 2018 W.P. Nos.16299 & 16310 of 2017 1 HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH: BENCH AT INDORE W.P. Nos.16299/2017 & 16310/2017 M/s Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of M.P. & Others Indore, dated 15.01.2018
texts.facts: This common order shall govern disposal of W.P. No.16299/2017 & W.P. No.16310/2017. The petitioner before this Court is a company registered under the Companies Act and is aggrieved by order dated 16.05.2016 passed by Designated Officer, Food and Durg Administration, District-Dewas, in Case No.21/FSSA/15-16. The petitioner is also aggrieved by order dated 12.08.2016 passed by the Adjudicating Officer, District-Dewas, in Case No.20/FSSA/15-16. The facts of the case reveal that the petitioner company is registered under the Companies Act and is manufacturer of Hakka Noodles Chowmein Miracle with Masala as provided under Section 22 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 r/w Regulation 2.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011. The petitioner's contention is that the Food Safety Officer, District-Dewas picked up certain samples of Ching's secret Hakka Noodles Chowmein Miracle with Masala from the premises of M/s Pakiza Retail Pvt. Ltd., A.V. Road, Dewas on 06.06.2015 and issued a notice in Form VA under Rule 2.4.1(3) of the Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011. The Food Sefety Officer has submitted the sample for analysis to the Food Analyst, State Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal and the sample was subjected to examination. In its report, the laboratory vide report dated 21.12.2015 has categorically given a report that no MSG is added. The sample was sent to the laboratory and the report of the laboratory also does not reveal the detection of any Mono-Sodium Glutamate (MSG). In similar circumstances, in case of ITC Limited (supra), the ITC Limited was again being prosecuted for mentioning "NO MSG ADDED" and co-ordinate Bench of this Court has passed a detailed and exhaustive order in W.P. No.5427/2016. Paragraph-2 to 21 of the aforesaid judgment reads as under:- 2/ In brief, the petitioner's case is that it is engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing of various packaged products including 'noodles' and 'pasta' under the brand name 'Sunfeast'. The Food Safety Officer, Dewas had taken sample of 'Sunfeast Yippee Noodles Magic Masala' from retail premises of M/s Neelkamal Multi Trade Pvt. Ltd. on 1.6.2015 and had issued notice in Form VA under Rule 2.4.1 (3) of Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011 to the retailer only. The sample was submitted for analysis to the Food Analyst, State Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal and the report dated 4.7.2015 was obtained, in which no Monosodium Glutamate (MSG) was detected yet the Food Analyst in the reprot dated 22.12.2015 declared the samples to be misbranded on the ground that mentioning of 'No MSG Added' is misleading under Regulation 2.3(1)(5) of the Packaging and Labelling Regulation. The further case of the petitioner is that sanction for prosecution was wrongly granted by order dated 28.5.2016 by the designated officer and in pursuance to the said sanction the Food Safety Officer, Dewas had preferred a complaint before the Court of Additional District Magistrate-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Dewas alleging violation of Section 26(1),(2)(ii)(v), 3(zf)(A)(i), of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulation 2.3(1)(5) of the Packaging and Labelling Regulation and being liable under Section 27(1) of the Act and punishable under Section 52 and Section 58 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. The petitioner was issued notice by the M/S Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd. vs Food And Drug Administration Dewas on 15 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34019947/ 2 Adjudicating Authority and the petitioner by appearing before the Adjudicating Authority had filed objection with respect to the maintainability of the complaint and prayed for dropping the proceedings on the ground that charge was not made out. By the order dated 26.7.2016 the Adjudicating Officer has rejected the objection and has held the complaint to be maintainable.
texts.arguments: However, it has been observed that the sample has been misbranded. Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued before this Court that only declaration, which is creating problem in his cases is that the company has mentioned over the product that no MSG is added. He has vehemently argued before this Court that it was not at all established that the MSG was added and in those circumstances, the question of misbranding, as alleged, doesn't arise. He has prayed for quashment of impugned orders, which are subject matter of the present petitions. He has also drawn the attention of this Court toward the judgment delivered in the case of ITC Limited Vs. M/S Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd. vs Food And Drug Administration Dewas on 15 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34019947/ 1 State of M.P. & Others in W.P. No.5427/2016, which was also delivered by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in similar circumstances. On the other hand, the learned Government Advocate has argued before this Court that by printing over the product that it does not contain MSG, the samples have been misbranded and as the samples have been misbranded, they have rightly initiated action against the petitioner under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 r/w Regulation 2.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2011. However, it has not been disputed by the learned Government Advocate that the report submitted by the laboratory does not reveal that any MSG was added by the manufacturer i.e. the petitioner company. A prayer has been made for dismissal of the writ petition. Undisputedly, the petitioner before this Court has stated categorically over the food products manufactured by him that no MSG has been added by him. 3/ Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since no MSG was detected in the laboratory test of the sample, therefore, it is not a case of misbranding. He further submits that the petitioner had neither added MSG nor its natural presence was found, therefore, prosecution cannot be sustained. He has also submitted that the sanction was granted by the concerned authority mechanically without application of mind. 4/ As against this, learned counsel for the respondents has supported the impugned action submitting that the petitioner had mentioned in the label that "No MSG Added" which was misleading since no negative declaration could be given and the petitioner could only mention the contents which were present on the label and could not have mentioned the contents which were not present.
